label: site test
goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

outcome.reason: Reached the payment step. Stopped there: nothing was paid.

findings.problem: [name] banner buttons were reachable only after tabbing past an accessibility button and a Learn more link; opening Preferences left no keyboard focus inside the consent dialog, so I had to tab again to find Reject all.

Many tab stops in the product grid and carousel have no name (unnamed links and buttons) and slide dots read only as Go to slide 1 and 2, so I could not tell what they do; I had to tab through about 10 stops before reaching a product button.

Each product card has an Add to Wishlist icon button plus an image link and a name link before the add to bag button, so reaching the next product takes 4 tab presses and the home page has no way to jump to a product.

After pressing add to bag there was no spoken or visible confirmation and the cart count still read 0; focus silently jumped to a Close button of a cart drawer that I could not perceive until I tabbed on.

In the cart drawer the check out button sits after the item controls, three promotional upsell product cards (each with unnamed links and add to bag buttons) and a discount code field, so I needed about 15 tab presses and risked adding extra items by mistake before reaching check out.
